Sequence: grant; one deliberately forbidden proposal (concession 51 bps > 50 bps policy maximum) that the mandate must refuse; one valid trade of 1 USDC, filled and settled; a second signed order of 0.5 USDC that is withheld (bundle simulated, not sent); revoke; relay of the withheld bundle, which passes only if the verifier rejects it for the removed key before its deadline with both nonces unused and balances unchanged; recovery of both assets to the owner's Intents account.

Grant policy: PROPOSED, pending the owner's policy decision; not adopted. SPEC.md requires an oracle maximum age of 60 seconds and proposes a deadline no later than 60 seconds after authorization; Policy::DEMO uses 60/60. This template proposes order_ttl_sec 120 and oracle_max_age_sec 120 for the mainnet run only, as an explicit deviation the owner must accept in the approval; otherwise set both to 60. An order's deadline is min(now + order_ttl, oldest price publish time + oracle_max_age); 60 s leaves too little time on mainnet for MPC signing, revocation to FINAL and the relay, so the revocation test would likely be inconclusive. Trade-off: prices up to 120 s old are accepted and a signed order stays executable up to 120 s while revocation is pending. The proposal charge is 1000 bps instead of the spec's proposed 50 bps default (Policy::DEMO, 200 records per grant), so the record bound fits the funded storage; it consumes authorization capacity only, at least 10% of the initial value per proposal, and the run's three proposals fit within the turnover cap. Every cap is unchanged.

Budget caps: owner inventory <= 5 USDC + 1.25 wNEAR (about $10 at NEAR ~= $4.0 on 2026-11-04); single order <= 1 USDC; mandate sales <= 2 USDC in total (the refused 0.5 USDC is counted conservatively); filler pays <= 0.5 wNEAR in total (the withheld relay is counted conservatively). Recompute the wNEAR units from the price on the approval day.

Deployment, storage and all funding are done separately by the owner under the approved setup record; this runner never funds, deposits or deploys. The grant's proposal_charge_bps 1000 bounds one grant to turnover_cap_bps / proposal_charge_bps = 10 order records (SPEC.md rule 9), so at the template's 1000-byte order records the mandate meets the per-grant storage rule with about 3.3 NEAR and no storage deviation (R1 checks the exact rule against the real storage_usage).

The worst-case fee of the steps below at gas price 1e8 yocto is (sum over transaction steps of the step's gas_tgas + 5) x 1e12 x 1e8 = 1310 TGas = 0.131 NEAR; max_fee_yocto is 0.15 NEAR. Preflight refuses if the live gas price makes the worst case exceed it.

Run: MANDATE_LIVE=1 MANDATE_LIVE_MANIFEST=<this file> MANDATE_LIVE_CONFIRM=<sha256 of this file> make live. Resume after a stop: add MANDATE_LIVE_RESUME=1 (reconciles the ledger in out/live/<sha256>/ first).

Mandate code hash 7dzGdFk3UaY9m3eQedMaiN2tjnxcp1awe1gdo5MH4ywV is the reproducible build of 163ccfa (fixtures/deploy/bounded_mandate-163ccfa-reproducible.wasm, sha256 629fc90f...); a mainnet manifest must name a pinned fixtures/deploy build.

Preflight also requires: verifier fee 1 pip, both oracle prices fresh and within confidence, MPC derived_public_key for the next grant path, agent allowance <= 0.25 NEAR, owner free NEAR >= worst-case fees + 0.5 NEAR reserve, mandate free NEAR >= expected storage, no active grant (expect_existing_grant false) and no unlisted open orders.

Owner key list (expected_owner_keys, required on mainnet): every access key of accounts.owner as returned by view_access_key_list at approval time, one entry per key with its permission ("full_access", or {receiver_id, method_names}) and nonce. A fresh start refuses any difference. During the run and on every resume, any added or removed key, changed permission, or nonce change of a key the ledger does not track (any key other than keys.owner) stops the run; before every runner-signed transaction the signing key's nonce must equal the ledger's expectation, so an owner transaction the ledger does not record is never absorbed.
